{{Short description|Concept in mathematics and theoretical physics}}
In [[mathematics]] and [[theoretical physics]], the '''Eguchi–Hanson space''' is a non-compact, [[self-dual]], asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) metric on the [[cotangent bundle]] of the 2-sphere ''T''<sup>*</sup>''S''<sup>2</sup>. The [[holonomy group]] of this 4-real-dimensional [[manifold]] is SU(2). The metric is generally attributed to the physicists [[Tohru Eguchi]] and [[Andrew J. Hanson]]; it was discovered independently by the mathematician [[Eugenio Calabi]] around the same time in 1979.<ref name="eguchi">{{cite journal|last=Eguchi|first=Tohru|author2=Hanson, Andrew J.|title=Selfdual solutions to Euclidean gravity|journal=Annals of Physics|year=1979|volume=120|issue=1|pages=82–105|url=http://www.slac.stanford.edu/cgi-wrap/getdoc/slac-pub-2213.pdf|bibcode = 1979AnPhy.120...82E |doi = 10.1016/0003-4916(79)90282-3 |osti=1447072}}</ref><ref name="calabi">{{cite journal|last=Calabi|first=Eugenio|title=Métriques kählériennes et fibrés holomorphes|journal=Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure|year=1979|volume=Quatrième Série, 12|issue=2|pages=269–294|doi=10.24033/asens.1367|url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASENS_1979_4_12_2_269_0|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The Eguchi-Hanson metric  has  [[Ricci tensor]] equal to zero, making it a solution to the vacuum [[Einstein's equations|Einstein equations]] of general relativity, albeit with Riemannian rather than Lorentzian [[metric signature]]. It may be regarded as a [[resolution of singularities|resolution]] of the ''A''<sub>1</sub> singularity according to the [[ADE classification]] which is the singularity at the fixed point of the ''C''<sup>2</sup>/''Z''<sub>2</sub> [[orbifold]] where the ''Z''<sub>2</sub> group inverts the signs of both complex coordinates in&nbsp;''C''<sup>2</sup>. The even dimensional space ''C''<sup>d/2</sup>/''Z''<sub>d/2</sub> of (real-)dimension <math>d</math> can be described using complex coordinates <math>w_i \in \mathbb C^{d/2}</math> with a metric

:<math>
g_{i \bar j} = \bigg(1+\frac{\rho^d}{r^{d}}\bigg)^{2/d}\bigg[\delta_{i\bar j}-\frac{\rho^d \bar w_i  w_{\bar j}}{r^2(\rho^d+r^{d})}\bigg],
</math>

where <math>\rho</math> is a scale setting constant and <math>r^2 = |w|^2_{\mathbb C^{d/2}}</math>.

Aside from its inherent importance in pure [[geometry]], the space is important in [[string theory]]. Certain types of [[K3 surface]]s can be approximated as a combination of several Eguchi–Hanson metrics since both have the same holonomy group. Similarly, the space can also be used to construct [[Calabi–Yau manifold]]s by replacing the orbifold singularities of <math>T^6/\mathbb Z_3</math> with Eguchi–Hanson spaces.<ref>{{cite book|last=Polchinski|first=J.|author-link=Joseph Polchinski|date=1998|title=String Theory Volume II: Superstring Theory and Beyond|url=|doi=|location=|publisher=Cambridge University Press|chapter=17|page=309-310|isbn=978-1551439761}}</ref>

The Eguchi–Hanson metric is the prototypical example of a [[gravitational instanton]]; detailed expressions for the metric are given in that article. It is then an example of a [[hyperkähler manifold]].<ref name="calabi" />
